question: Using Section 4J.03 and Figure 4J-3, give the full pedestrian-hybrid-beacon sequence and identify which stage corresponds to the pedestrian walk interval.
model_answer: Direct Answer: The pedestrian hybrid beacon sequence is: (1) dark until activated, (2) flashing yellow upon pedestrian actuation, (3) steady yellow, (4) both steady red indications, (5) alternating flashing red, and (6) dark again until the next actuation. The pedestrian walk interval corresponds to stage 4 — both steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications — during which the pedestrian signal heads display the WALKING PERSON (WALK) indication. Standards (mandatory): - "Pedestrian hybrid beacon indications shall be dark (not illuminated) during periods between actuations." - "Following an actuation by a pedestrian, a pedestrian hybrid beacon face shall display a flashing CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by a steady CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by both steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian walk interval, followed by alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian change interval (see Figure 4J-3)." Upon termination of the pedestrian change interval, "the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces shall revert to a dark (not illuminated) condition." - "The pedestrian signal heads shall display a WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication when the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces are displaying steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications. The pedestrian signal heads shall display a flashing UPRAISED HAND (symbolizing DONT WALK) signal indication when the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces are displaying alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications." - "The duration of the steady yellow change interval shall be determined using engineering practices in accordance with the provisions in Section 4F.17." - "A pedestrian hybrid beacon face shall consist of three signal sections, with a CIRCULAR YELLOW signal indication centered below two horizontally-aligned CIRCULAR RED signal indications (see Figure 4J-3)." Options (permitted): - Per the note in Figure 4J-3: an optional steady red clearance interval may be added after Interval 3, and an optional short buffer interval (alternating flashing red while the pedestrian signal heads are displaying a steady UPRAISED HAND) may be added after Interval 5. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 4J-3 depicts the six-stage sequence — 1. Dark Until Activated; 2. Flashing Yellow Upon Activation; 3. Steady Yellow; 4. Steady Red During Pedestrian Walk Interval; 5. Alternating Flashing Red During Pedestrian Change Interval; 6. Dark Again Until Activated — explicitly labeling stage 4 as the pedestrian walk interval. - [Image 2] Page 770 shows Figure 4J-3 in page context along with related Section 4J.02 provisions and the start of Section 4J.03 operation standards. - [Image 3] Page 768 provides Section 4J.01 application provisions and Figure 4J-1 installation guidelines for low-speed roadways (context only). - [Image 4] Page 769 provides Figure 4J-2 and the Section 4J.02 design standard requiring the three-section beacon face configuration shown in Figure 4J-3. - [Image 5] Page 759 shows Chapter 4I pedestrian signal head indications (WALKING PERSON and UPRAISED HAND) that operate in conjunction with the beacon sequence. Citations: - Section 4J.03 Standard §1 (p.729) - Section 4J.03 Standard §2 (p.730) - Section 4J.03 Standard §3 (p.730) - Section 4J.03 Standard §10 (p.730) - Section 4J.02 Standard §2 (p.728) - Section 4J.02 Guidance §4 (p.729) - Figure 4J-3 (p.729)
gold_answer: Dark, flashing yellow, steady yellow, both steady red, alternating flashing red, then dark. The both-steady-red stage corresponds to the pedestrian walk interval.
